title: Wave Race: Blue Storm
subtitle: Nintendo Software Technology · GameCube

body: Wave Race: Blue Storm is Nintendo Software Technology's GameCube water-racing game, following Wave Race 64 with new courses, riders and changing weather. Personal watercraft race around buoys while waves continually alter the surface beneath them. The next turn is therefore affected by more than the shape of a fixed track. A swell can lift the craft or disturb an approach, requiring the player to read the water as part of the route. The race remains a contest against other riders, but the sea is an active participant in every lap.

Championship events provide a weather forecast for their successive days, and the player chooses the order in which available courses are raced. A difficult venue may be more manageable in calmer conditions, making planning part of the sporting challenge before the start. Correctly passing coloured buoys builds the turbo meter, while a missed buoy costs that accumulated progress. The rider balances the prescribed route against opportunities to accelerate, with the weather influencing how confidently a familiar sequence of corners can be attempted.

Released with the GameCube in Japan in 2001, Blue Storm gave the console a showcase for a landscape that moves beneath the player. Different riders bring their own handling characteristics, and multiplayer lets a group contest the courses together. Lawrence Schwedler and James Phillipsen composed the music. Its central pleasure remains learning how to cooperate with an unstable surface. A fast lap depends on making the machine work with the water's movement, recognising when to commit to a turn and when the next wave requires an adjustment.
